'''Micha Asher Perles''' ({{Langx|he|מיכה פרלס}}) is an Israeli mathematician working in geometry, a professor emeritus at the [[Hebrew University]].<ref>[http://www.huji.ac.il/dataj/controller/ihoker/MOP-STAFF_LINK?sno=300498 Faculty profile], Hebrew University, retrieved 2013-12-12.</ref> He earned his Ph.D. in 1964 from the Hebrew University, under the supervision of [[Branko Grünbaum]].<ref name="mg">{{MathGenealogy|id=58897}}</ref>
His contributions include:
*The [[Perles configuration]], a set of nine points in the [[Euclidean plane]] whose collinearities can be realized only by using irrational numbers as coordinates. Perles used this configuration to prove the existence of irrational [[polytope]]s in higher dimensions.<ref>{{citation
 | last = Grünbaum | first = Branko | authorlink = Branko Grünbaum
 | edition = Second
 | isbn = 0-387-00424-6
 | location = New York
 | mr = 1976856
 | pages = 93–95
 | publisher = Springer-Verlag
 | series = Graduate Texts in Mathematics
 | title = Convex polytopes
 | title-link = Convex Polytopes
 | volume = 221
 | year = 2003}}.</ref>
*The [[Perles–Sauer–Shelah lemma]], a result in [[extremal set theory]] whose proof was credited to Perles by [[Saharon Shelah]].<ref>{{citation
 | last = Shelah | first = Saharon
 | journal = Pacific Journal of Mathematics
 | mr = 0307903
 | pages = 247–261
 | title = A combinatorial problem; stability and order for models and theories in infinitary languages
 | url = http://projecteuclid.org/getRecord?id=euclid.pjm/1102968432
 | volume = 41
 | year = 1972
 | doi=10.2140/pjm.1972.41.247| doi-access = free
 }}.</ref><ref>{{citation|url=http://gilkalai.wordpress.com/2008/09/28/extremal-combinatorics-iii-some-basic-theorems/|first=Gil|last=Kalai|authorlink=Gil Kalai|title=Extremal Combinatorics III: Some Basic Theorems|work=Combinatorics and More|date=September 28, 2008}}.</ref>
*The [[pumping lemma for context-free languages]], a widely used method for proving that a language is not [[Context-free language|context-free]] that Perles discovered with [[Yehoshua Bar-Hillel]] and [[Eli Shamir]].<ref>{{citation|title=The New Turing Omnibus: Sixty-Six Excursions in Computer Science|first=A. K.|last=Dewdney|authorlink=Alexander Dewdney|publisher=Macmillan|year=1993|page=91|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=NDiU62j7jeMC&pg=PA91|isbn=9780805071665}}.</ref>
Notable students of Perles include [[Noga Alon]], [[Gil Kalai]], and [[Nati Linial]].<ref name="mg"/>
